newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Riksbank defends its forex control.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Riksbank defends its forex control.

text.p: Sweden's central bank said on Friday that an inquiry that has proposed taking responsibility for the exchange rate policy away from the bank could undermine credibility of monetary policy.
The recommendation for the forex policy responsibility to be shifted to the government was made in January by the Exchange Rate Policy Inquiry ordered by parliament.

"The proposals ... would be liable to undermine the credibility of monetary policy and thereby the Riksbank's ability to fulfil the objective of safeguarding the value of money," the bank said in a statement.
"That would tend to raise the level of interest rates and might also restrict the Riksbank's potential within the framework of a policy for price stability, for supporting general economic policy."

The Riksbank said it was inevitable the two fields of monetary and exchange rate policy could conflict in a world of deregulated financial markets and free capital flow where markets for money and currencies were directly interlinked.
"An indistinct assignment of responsibility may impair confidence in monetary policy and the objective of price stability," the bank said.
"A high degree of credibility as regards monetary policy and the price stability objective is, in the opinion of the board, particularly important if Sweden were to stay outside the euro area."
The Riksbank said the government should decide the exchange rate regime for the crown in relation to other European Union currencies.
But the bank should decide how to operate this exchange rate regime in order to sustain confidence in monetary policy and the price stability objective.
"The means that decisions about a central rate and the band width in a fixed exchange rate system are to be made by the Riksbank," the bank said.
"Contrary to the inquiry's proposals, it also means that the government shall not be in a position to issue general guidelines for exchange rate policy with a flexible exchange rate."
